title: Weekend Rejections and Recollection Time — Laboratory Test Orders
content:
The day of the week on which a Laboratory Test Orders specimen was most recently rejected lengthens its recollection window.

When the date of the most recent specimen rejection on the accession falls on a Saturday, the recollection window is lengthened by **2 days**. When it falls on a Sunday, the window is lengthened by **1 day**. A rejection dated Monday to Friday receives no weekend lengthening.

| Most recent rejection dated on | Lengthening |
|---|---|
| Saturday | 2 days |
| Sunday | 1 day |
| Monday to Friday | none |

The weekday is read from the ordinary calendar, on which 1 January 2024 fell on a Monday. Holidays play no part: a rejection on a weekday holiday receives no weekend lengthening.

**Examples (hypothetical dates).**

- Rejection dated Saturday 8 March 2025: 2 days.
- Rejection dated Sunday 9 March 2025: 1 day.
- Rejection dated Monday 10 March 2025: none.
- An accession rejected on a Saturday and again on the following Tuesday: only the most recent rejection (the Tuesday) counts, so there is no weekend lengthening.
